en.title: Dark Link Finally Revealed in Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Remake Trailers
en.summary: Nintendo has dropped new trailers for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, giving fans their first official look at the iconic Dark Link. The shadowy doppelgänger appears in what promises to be a faithful recreation of one of the game's most memorable boss fights.
en.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is slowly but surely coming into focus for eager fans, and the latest Nintendo trailers offer a tantalizing glimpse at one of the original game's most memorable adversaries: Dark Link. These brief but impactful TV spots, released for the Japanese market, showcase not just updated visuals but also key moments that have defined Link's epic journey through time.

For those who braved the treacherous dungeons of the N64 classic, Dark Link needs no introduction. He is the spectral, mirror-image doppelgänger of Link, serving as the formidable mini-boss of the notoriously challenging Water Temple. The encounter takes place in a mist-shrouded chamber, where shallow water and a solitary dead tree set a haunting scene. What made this battle particularly brilliant was its dynamic nature: Dark Link's name mirrored the player's save file name, and his health bar precisely matched Link's current number of Heart Containers. The new trailers confirm this fight is making a return, with footage showing Dark Link materializing on Link's sword, his menacing gaze fixed on his heroic counterpart.

> "Fans of the original game will know Dark Link well. He’s a shadowy, mirror-image doppelgänger of Link who serves as the mini-boss of Ocarina’s iconic Water Temple."

Beyond the chilling appearance of Dark Link, these trailers also offer further delights. We catch sight of the formidable Ganondorf at an organ, Link masterfully playing his ocarina, and the pivotal cutscene where Link finally draws the Master Sword. For newcomers, these trailers might indeed venture into spoiler territory, offering a comprehensive look at some of the game's most significant plot points. The visual overhaul promises to bring Hyrule to life with stunning detail, a significant upgrade from the original's groundbreaking, yet dated, graphics.

## A Mirror to the Player's Journey

The reveal of Dark Link is more than just a cosmetic update; it's a nod to the intricate design that made **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** a landmark title. The way Dark Link's health dynamically scaled with the player's progress was a stroke of genius, making each encounter feel personal and challenging. Early reports suggest the remake will cleverly utilize environmental reflections to foreshadow Dark Link's appearance, a subtle yet effective touch that enhances the build-up to this iconic boss battle. This attention to detail reassures long-time fans that the heart of the original experience is being preserved, even as the visuals are modernized.

## What's Next

The **Ocarina of Time** remake is slated for release on the **Nintendo Switch 2** on November 5, 2026. With these trailers offering a clear look at Dark Link and other key moments, anticipation is building for a faithful yet visually spectacular return to one of gaming's most beloved worlds.

content_raw: As Nintendo has pulled back the curtain on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , we’ve begun to get a better understanding of how this Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive will look and feel to play. IGN has already got you covered with an extensive hands-on preview , as well as a roundup of all the changes we’ve noticed so far compared to the N64 masterpiece. But now, Nintendo has released two new trailers (TV spots for Japan) that, while brief, reveal a tantalizing glimpse at some never-before-seen characters, chief among them Dark Link. Potential spoilers for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake follow… Fans of the original game will know Dark Link well. He’s a shadowy, mirror-image doppelgänger of Link who serves as the mini-boss of Ocarina’s iconic Water Temple. You fight him in a fog-filled room with shallow water and a dead tree in the center, in what is one of the more memorable battles in the game. Brilliantly, Dark Link’s name mirrors the player's save file name (as registered by Navi), and his total health scales dynamically to match the exact number of Heart Containers Link has at that moment. The new trailer shows this fight in action, although we only get the briefest of looks at how it plays out. We see Dark Link leak onto Link’s sword, looking down menacingly at our hero. Dark Link isn’t the only thing worth highlighting about these two videos. We see big bad guy Ganondorf playing an organ, Link playing his Ocarina, the cutscene where Link finally gets the Master Sword, and plenty more. Indeed, I’d say these trailers veer into spoiler territory if you’ve never played Ocarina of Time before, which is why I’ve slapped this article with a spoiler warning up top. As a huge fan of the original game, there isn’t really anything here that would spoil my enjoyment, but we do see some endgame footage. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026. While you wait, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview.
